strengths: Novel empirical finding of local, asynchronous grokking in practical LLM pretraining, contrasting with prior work's global synchronous grokking

Practical utility: Zero-cost metrics (pathway distance and consistency) that strongly correlate with downstream task performance (0.97+ correlations) without requiring instruction tuning or benchmarking
Well-designed experiments with careful methodology: Min-K%++ contamination detection, bipartite matching for data grouping, clear separation of pretraining/test/validation sets
Strong empirical validation across four diverse domains (math, code, commonsense, domain-specific) with clear visualizations demonstrating layer-wise routing dynamics
Mechanistic interpretation linking memorization-to-generalization transition to routing pathway evolution with interpretable depth-dependent patterns
Theoretical grounding via generalization bound (Theorem 4.1) connecting routing complexity to generalization, with empirical validation of edit distance-effective dimension correlation
Clear and significant comparison to baseline metrics showing conventional pretraining losses fail to capture the memorization-to-generalization transition
weaknesses: Limited scope: Study restricted to single model (OLMoE, 7B); generalization to other MoE models and dense architectures (which are more common in practice) remains unclear
Theory-practice gap: Generalization bound assumes fixed routing and NTK regime, but OLMoE uses learned/adaptive routing during pretraining; mismatch weakens theoretical contribution
Pathway metrics design choices not fully justified: expert selection threshold, pathway consistency normalization, memorization definition (ε, δ) lack ablation studies and sensitivity analysis
Data grouping via SentenceTransformer embeddings for bipartite matching introduces dependence on embedding model choice; potential circularity with downstream tasks
Evaluation limitations: Only 10 equidistant checkpoints sampled (coarse sampling), only 4 domains, focus on checkpoints after accuracy rise could introduce selection bias
Reproducibility concerns: Code availability not mentioned; key implementation details in appendices; some hyperparameter choices lack justification
Theory limitations: Generalization bound derived for one-layer MoE; extension to 16-layer OLMoE not formally addressed; Figure 8 uses synthetic data, not validating practical applicability
